Captures whether at a given time horizon a company's revenue growth potential from climate transition opportunities can offset revenue losses due to activities that stand to lose, as estimated by BloombergNEF (BNEF).

The time horizon defaults to 2030 but can be overridden.

The climate scenario defaults to the baseline Economic Transition Scenario (ETS) in BNEF's New Energy Outlook but other climate scenarios, such as those published by the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), can be applied through overrides.

The field is available for every year until the end of the projection period and ranges from:
 - Very low risk (projected revenue gains are more than four times the losses, and the losses do not exceed 10% of the company revenue in the reference year)
 - Low risk (gains are more than twice the losses, and the losses do not exceed 30%)
 - Medium risk (losses are lower than the gains and do not exceed 50%)
 - High risk (losses are higher than the gains and do not exceed 70%
 - Very high risk (losses are twice the gains or exceed 70%)

The data used for the calculation is available through the fields Climate Transition Revenue Projection (ET094, CLIMATE_TRANS_REVENUE_PROJECTION) and Climate Transition Revenue Percentage Change (ET095, CLIMATE_TRANS_REVENUE_PCT_CHANGE).

Provides the name of the unique Bloomberg Specified Cohort Waterfall Level 1 ‘category’ or Level 2 ‘type’ to which a pool belongs. Applies to agency pools and cohorts.

By default, this field returns the unique Level 2 specified pool type to which a pool belongs for the most recent available factor date. It returns the unique Level 1 category for Level 1 waterfall spec cohorts. It returns the unique Level 2 type for Level 2 waterfall spec cohorts. It returns a blank value for coupon/vintage cohorts and non-waterfall spec cohorts.

This field accepts overrides for Specified Cohort Waterfall Level (AN202, SPEC_COHORT_WATERFALL_LEVEL) and Mtge Collateral As of Date (DS538, MTG_COLLAT_DT).

The specified cohort waterfall partitions standard coupon/vintage cohorts into subsets that reflect historical Mortgage Backed Security (MBS) trading practices and aggregate to the overall cohort. The waterfall has two levels.  Level 1 partitions a coupon/vintage cohort into specified pool categories. Where applicable, Level 2 partitions Level 1 categories into more tightly defined specified pool types or stories. For Level 1 categories with no Level 2 partition, the Level 2 type is set to match the Level 1 category. The order of the waterfall progresses from loan characteristics with historically higher to lower pay-ups over To-Be-Announced (TBA) MBS prices.

While a pool may satisfy the inclusion criteria for multiple waterfall categories and types, it is allocated to the first/highest specified pool category and type for which it qualifies. If a pool does not meet the criteria of any specified pool category then it is assigned to a residual, worst-to-deliver, category with more TBA-like loan characteristics.

For Uniform Mortgage Backed Securities (UMBS), the set of Level 1 waterfall categories includes, in order: Low Loan Balance (LB), High Loan-to-Value Ratio (LTV), Specified Geography (GEO), Non-Owner Occupancy (OCC), Low Credit Score (FICO), and Worst-to-Deliver (W2D).

For Ginnie Mae (GNMA) MBS, the set of Level 1 waterfall categories includes, in order: Low Loan Balance (LB), Specified Geography (GEO), Rural Housing (RHS), GNMA HARP (HARP), Other GNMA 2 Custom Pools (G2OTHER), and Worst-to-Deliver (W2D).

Rating assigned by combining a portfolio's Corporate Sustainability Rating and Sovereign Sustainability Rating proportional to the relative weight of the (long only) corporate and sovereign positions, rounded to the nearest whole number. Sovereign Historical Sustainability Scores and Corporate Historical Sustainability Scores are ranked and rated separately, to represent the Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) risk of the portfolio relative to its peers for its respective corporate and sovereign positions, and then combined by their relative weights for the Portfolio Sustainability Rating.
 
 Morningstar assigns Corporate and Sovereign Sustainability Ratings by ranking the respective Corporate and Sovereign Historical Sustainability Scores of all scored funds within a Morningstar Global Category. ranked funds are divided into five groups, based on a normal distribution, and each receives a rating from "High" to "Low." For each peer group, the median scoring portfolio receives a '3' rating. Ratings are assigned to other portfolios in the peer group to achieve a normal distribution, with an exception made for cases where the scores within the peer group are not meaningfully differentiated. In practice this can mean that all portfolios within some peer groups may receive the same corporate or sovereign rating. Please note that lower risk results in a higher rating. Higher ratings indicate that a fund is, on average, invested in fewer companies or sovereign debt with a high ESG risk under Sustainalytics' ESG Risk and Country Risk methodologies, and therefore exposed to less risk driven by E, S or G factors.

fieldInfo.description: MS ESG FR Port Corp Sust Rtg
fieldInfo.documentation:
Rating assigned by ranking all scored funds within a Morningstar Global Category by their Historical Corporate Sustainability Scores. The ranked funds are then divided into five groups, based on a normal distribution, and each receives a rating from "High" to "Low." For each peer group, the median scoring portfolio receives a '3' rating. Ratings are assigned to other portfolios in the peer group to achieve a normal distribution, with an exception made for cases where the scores within the peer group are not meaningfully differentiated. In practice this can mean that all portfolios within some peer groups may receive the same corporate or sovereign rating. Please note that lower risk results in a higher rating. Higher ratings indicate that a fund is, on average, invested in fewer companies or sovereign debt with a high Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) risk under Sustainalytics' ESG Risk and Country Risk methodologies, and therefore exposed to less risk driven by E, S or G factors. Indicates whether or not the market operator has signaled that an aggressive order has been entered that, were it to be executed, would breach the prescribed trading limits that have been imposed on the security. Currently the field is available for SGX (Singapore Exchange), SEHK (Stock Exchange of Hong Kong) and TAIFEX (Taiwan Future Exchange).

On SGX (Singapore Exchange) and SEHK (Stock Exchange of Hong Kong), such an order will be rejected and the 'Circuit Breaker Trigger Signal' will be set to Yes/Y/true. The signal will remain for a minimum of five minutes. All other aggressive orders that do not breach the trading limit will continue to be accepted/executed. Consequently, the presence of this signal does not in itself indicate that trading on the security has been halted.

On SGX and SEHK, the applicable trading limits are only advertised during the 5-minute period known as the Dynamic Circuit Breaker for SGX or the Volatility Control Mechanism (VCM) for SEHK, identified by this field. The trading limits are available in the Minimum Dynamic Trading Limit Price (P1850, MIN_DYNAMIC_TRADING_LIMIT_PX) and Maximum Dynamic Trading Limit Price (P1851, MAX_DYNAMIC_TRADING_LIMIT_PX) fields. SGX will update this field to No/N/false once the Dynamic Circuit Breaker period has concluded. However, SEHK will not update this field to No/N/false once the Volatility Control Mechanism (VCM) has concluded. Reference price against which the Minimum Dynamic Trading Limit Price (P1850, MIN_DYNAMIC_TRADING_LIMIT_PX), and the Maximum Dynamic Trading Limit Price (P1851, MAX_DYNAMIC_TRADING_LIMIT_PX), are calculated.

On most execution venues, the dynamic trading limits are limits that are anchored to a dynamically updating reference price during the trading session, such as the Last Trade (RQ088, LAST_TRADE) price. Static trading limits, on the other hand, are anchored against a more static reference price such as the Official Closing Price (RQ429, PX_OFFICIAL_CLOSE_RT) price.

On SGX (Singapore Exchange) and SEHK (Stock Exchange of Hong Kong), this field is populated with the reference price against which the Dynamic Circuit Breaker on SGX and the Volatility Control Mechanism (VCM) on SEHK are triggered, the trigger being disclosed via Circuit Breaker Trigger Signal (P2104, CIRCUIT_BREAKER_TRIG_SIGNAL). These mechanisms are triggered when an order has been entered that, were it to be executed, would breach the prescribed trading limits that have been imposed on the security.

For SEHK, the reference price is the last trade price from 5 minutes prior to the current time.

For SGX, the reference price is defined as follows:
(a) first reference price of the trading day - this is determined in the following sequence: Equilibrium price traded at market open, previous day last traded price, last available traded price. For ETFs, this is determined in the following sequence: equilibrium price traded at market open, previous day ETF RCP, previous day last traded price, last available traded price.
(b) on-going reference price - this is determined in the following sequence: current day last traded price as of five minutes ago, first reference price of the trading day.
(c) reference price after cooling off period - if there are trades done during the period, this will be calculated as described in (b) above. If there are no trades done during the period, the first trade will not be subjected to circuit breaker. The price of the first trade will then serve as the reference price for trading for the next five minutes. Thereafter, the reference price will be determined as described in (b) above.
(d) reference price following trading halt / suspension: this is determined in the following sequence: equilibrium price traded after lifting of trading halt/suspension, current day last traded price preceding trading halt/suspension, first reference price of the trading day.
(e) reference price for ES will have the same reference price as the underlying instruments.

Indicates whether the participant quote is executable within the context of the price band for the issue when used on local exchange codes (i.e. UQ, UN, UP, etc.) or describes the limit state of the National Best Bid and Offer with respect to the price band for the issue when used on the composite exchange code (i.e. US). The Limit Up-Limit Down (LULD) mechanism is intended to prevent trades in National Market System (NMS) securities from occurring outside of specified price bands.  The bands would be set at a percentage level above and below the average reference price of the security over the immediately preceding five minute period.  To accommodate more fundamental price moves, there would be a five minute trading pause - similar to the pause triggered by the current single-stock circuit breakers - only if trading is unable to occur within the specified price band after 15 seconds.  The price band is represented in the Minimum Limit Price (PR507, PX_MIN_LIMIT) and Maximum Limit Price (PR508, PX_MAX_LIMIT) fields.

fieldInfo.description: Circuit Breaker Trigger Signal Start Time
fieldInfo.documentation:
Time at which the Circuit Breaker Trigger Signal (P2104, CIRCUIT_BREAKER_TRIG_SIGNAL) had been invoked, which indicates that an aggressive order has been entered that, were it to be executed, would breach the prescribed trading limits that have been imposed on the security.

On SGX (Singapore Exchange) and SEHK (Stock Exchange of Hong Kong), such an order will be rejected and the Circuit Breaker Trigger Signal (P2104, CIRCUIT_BREAKER_TRIG_SIGNAL) will be set to Yes/Y/true. The signal will remain for a minimum of five minutes, and the expected end time for the signal will be available via the Circuit Breaker Trigger Signal End Time (P2160, CB_TRIGGER_SIGNAL_END_TIME) field. All other aggressive orders that do not breach the trading limit will continue to be accepted/executed. Consequently, the presence of the signal does not in itself indicate that trading on the security has been halted.

On SGX and SEHK, the applicable trading limits are only advertised during the 5-minute period known as the Dynamic Circuit Breaker for SGX or the Volatility Control Mechanism (VCM) for SEHK, which is identified by the Circuit Breaker Trigger Signal (P2104, CIRCUIT_BREAKER_TRIG_SIGNAL) field. The trading limits are available in the Minimum Dynamic Trading Limit Price (P1850, MIN_DYNAMIC_TRADING_LIMIT_PX) and Maximum Dynamic Trading Limit Price (P1851, MAX_DYNAMIC_TRADING_LIMIT_PX) fields. The Total Risks in the denominator includes the following factors (risks):

 1) General Insurance Risk: the risk of incurring claims payments which exceed the usual estimates.  That is, it is the difference between the estimated maximum claims payments based on probability and the estimated claims payments which form the foundation of the calculation of insurance premium rates.

 2) Expected Interest Rate Risk: the risk of actual interest rates falling below forecast due to substantial changes in the economic environment.

 - Risk of losses caused by price fluctuations, etc. in the value of stocks, real estate, and other assets.

4) Business Administration Risk: the risk of incurring losses caused by misjudgment, default, etc. of business administration.

fieldInfo.description: Event Trade MMT Level 1 Trade Type Code - Realtime
fieldInfo.documentation:
Market Model Typology (MMT) Level 1 (Market Mechanism) trade type code for MMT v1.0 and above.

MMT is an evolving standard for describing equity transactions on European markets. It is administered by the FIX Trading Community. For more information on MMT please reference: http://www.fixtradingcommunity.org/pg/group-types/mmt

This field is available only when trade events are received on a market data feed and it should be used in conjunction with the other MMT fields, all of which collectively describe the trade.

This field provides the MMT market mechanism, which defines the fundamental type of mechanism employed by the market in which the trade was facilitated and executed.

The possible values (MMT display codes) are:
CLOB (LB in MMT v4.2 and below) - Central Limit Order Book
QDTS (QB in MMT v4.2 and below) - Quote Driven Market
DABO (DB in MMT v4.2 and below) - Dark Order Book
VOIC (OB in MMT v4.2 and below) - Off Book (including Voice or Messaging Trading)
PATS (PA in MMT v4.2 and below) - Periodic Auction
RFQT (RQ in MMT v4.2 and below) - Request for Quotes
AHHY (AH in MMT v4.2 and below) - Any Other, Including Hybrid (original ESMA definition in RTSs 1 & 2)
HYBR (HS in MMT v4.2 and below) - Hybrid System (revised ESMA definition, replacing 'Any Other, Including Hybrid') [MMT v4.0 and above only]
OTHR (AO in MMT v4.2 and below) - Any Other, Excluding Hybrid (revised ESMA definition, replacing 'Any Other, Including Hybrid') [MMT v4.0 and above only)


More detailed definitions of each of these values now follow.

CLOB (LB in MMT v4.2 and below)- Central Limit Order Book:
A trading mechanism where buy and sell orders are entered onto on an electronically maintained and prioritized order book that automatically matches these orders. The book consists of lit (visible) orders but may also consist of partially or fully hidden orders, such as iceberg or large in scale (LIS) orders. If the order book is in a continuous trading phase, then matching buy and sell orders will be executed and reported as trades immediately. If the order book is in an auction call trading phase, during which orders are theoretically matched for execution at a continuously calculated equilibrium price that ensures the maximum possible executed volume, then the matching orders will be executed and reported at the conclusion of the auction call trading phase. Analogous with the following type(s) of trading system defined under RTS 1 and RTS 2 within MiFID II: 'Continuous auction order book trading system' and - for scheduled auction call trading phases only - 'Periodic auction trading system'.

QDTS (QB in MMT v4.2 and below) - Quote Driven Market:
A trading method by which execution prices are largely determined from buy and sell offer quotations issued by market makers or dealers. Most such systems operate a mandatory quotation period during each trading day, during which registered market makers must display their best buy and sell quotations. The market makers are obliged to transact at those quotations if approached to do so. Analogous with the following type(s) of trading system defined under RTS 1 and RTS 2 within MiFID II: 'Quote-driven trading system'.

DABO (DB in MMT v4.2 and below) - Dark Order Book:
A dark order book offers the similar or equivalent capabilities to a Central Limit Order Book, but only orders set to execute at the (mid-point) reference price interact with like orders via a real or virtual dark order trading facility. Orders are completely hidden which grants the traders full anonymity with Price formation derived from an external reference price.

VOIC (OB in MMT v4.2 and below) - Off Book (including Voice or Messaging Trading):
Trades that have not been executed on a quote-driven or order-driven book, or via a periodic auction or request for quotes market mechanism, are considered to be 'off book' trades. Analogous with the following type(s) of trading system defined under RTS 1 and RTS 2 within MiFID II: 'Voice trading system' and 'Any other trading system not covered by the other trading system descriptions'.

PATS (PA in MMT v4.2 and below) - Periodic Auction:
A trading mechanism where one or more auction calls is the sole method for generating executions and where the auction call is not facilitated by a Central Limit Order Book (CLOB). During the auction call, participants enter buy or sell quotations or orders that may influence an equilibrium price against which the maximum possible volume can be executed at the conclusion of the auction call. The time of the conclusion of the auction call may be predetermined or it may be triggered by specific conditions being satisfied in the market. Analogous with the following type(s) of trading system defined under RTS 1 and RTS 2 within MiFID II: 'Periodic auction trading system'.

RFQT (RQ in MMT v4.2 and below) - Request for Quotes:
A trading mechanism where a quote or quotes are sent in response to a 'request for quote' submitted by one or more members or participants. The quote is executable exclusively by the party initiating the request for quote and this execution is triggered by said party accepting the quote or quotes. Analogous with the following type(s) of trading system defined under RTS 1 and RTS 2 within MiFID II: 'Request for quote trading system'.

AHHY (AH in MMT v4.2 and below) - Any Other, Including Hybrid (original ESMA definition in RTSs 1 & 2):
Any other type of trading mechanism, including a hybrid of some of the above defined market mechanisms and/or price determination processes that facilitated the trade. Analogous with the following type(s) of trading system defined under RTS 1 and RTS 2 within MiFID II: 'Any other trading system' (RTS 1); 'Trading system not covered by the first 5 rows' (RTS 2).

HYBR (HS in MMT v4.2 and below) - Hybrid System (revised ESMA definition, replacing 'Any Other, Including Hybrid'):
A trading mechanism that uses a combination of some of the first 6 of the above defined trading mechanisms at the same time.

OTHR (AO in MMT v4.2 and below) - Any Other, Excluding Hybrid (revised ESMA definition, replacing 'Any Other, Including Hybrid'):
Any other type of trading mechanism, excluding the first 6 of the trading mechanisms defined above or the Hybrid System defined above.

This field should be referenced in conjunction with the other MMT fields in order to obtain a full MMT definition of the trade.
